root_cause: Top-level ready gating incorrectly ties mat_ready to pp_in_ready, while pp_in_ready is driven by output/backpressure state in mv_postproc. During matrix ingestion this creates a deadlock path that can keep mat_ready low and block all mat transfers.

first_divergence.expected: mat_ready should assert during COMPUTE_ROWS when matrix beats are expected (subject to control-state legality).
first_divergence.observed: mat_ready stays deasserted until send_beat timeout (SimTimeoutError: timeout waiting mat_ready).

evidence.observation: Failure at send_beat on mat channel with SimTimeoutError waiting mat_ready.
evidence.relevance: First authoritative functional failure after successful build/lint.

evidence.observation: Same timeout waiting mat_ready during matrix send.
evidence.relevance: Confirms systematic handshake bug, not data-dependent arithmetic mismatch.

evidence.observation: mat_ready is defined as ... && pp_in_ready; pp_in_ready originates from mv_postproc in_ready (depends on out_valid/out_ready).
evidence.relevance: Direct causal coupling of matrix ingress to output-side readiness can deadlock compute ingress.

evidence.observation: Matrix channel must support backpressure but accept beats during compute phase independently of unrelated channel deadlock; staged control requires phased progress.
evidence.relevance: Current coupling violates intended phased flow/handshake independence.

alternative_hypotheses: Potential control-counter desynchronization between mv_ctrl_fsm and top local counters.
Potential row_done/new_row alignment issue in MAC path causing downstream starvation.
